$comment: POST /v1.0/users/{userId}/onlineMeetings -- verified against Microsoft Learn's application-post-onlinemeetings reference 2026-09-16. The /users/{userId} form (rather than /me) is what an APPLICATION-permission bot calls; it needs a tenant administrator's application access policy naming that user (see the manifest's oauth $scopeComment), not just OAuth consent.
title: Create meeting
description: Create a Teams meeting on behalf of a user and get its join link.
$idempotencyComment: onlineMeetings has no documented idempotency key. A retry creates a SECOND meeting with its own id and join link, never returns the first.

config.label: User ID
config.description: The Microsoft Entra object id of the user the meeting is created on behalf of -- the one named in the application access policy a tenant admin granted this app.

config.label: Start
config.description: ISO 8601 with an offset or Z, e.g. 2026-09-22T14:00:00Z.

config.label: End
config.description: ISO 8601 with an offset or Z.

config.label: Require a passcode
config.description: Passcodes are auto-generated by Teams; a custom one is not supported. Leave off for no passcode.

outputShape.description: The meeting's id -- what meeting_get and transcript_list need.
The join link. Its format may change -- Microsoft's own docs say not to parse it.
When Graph created the meeting resource.
The organizer's user id -- should equal the userId that was asked for.
The numeric id shown in the Teams client to join by phone or the join screen.
Echoes what was asked, or Teams' default.
The auto-generated passcode when one was required; null otherwise.
